chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdul Malik al-Qummi, from Idrees his brother, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: When you have finished your prayer, say:

O Allah, I follow Your religion by Your obedience, and Your Wilayah, and the Wilayah of Your Messenger, and the Wilayah of the Imams (peace be upon them), from their first to their last, and I name them.

Then say: O Allah, I follow Your religion by Your obedience and their Wilayah, and pleasure with what You have preferred them with, without arrogance nor being arrogant against the meaning of what You revealed in Your Book, upon the limits of what reached us regarding it and what did not reach us, believing, accepting, submitting to that, pleased with what You are pleased with.

O Lord, I intend Your Face and the Hereafter by it, fearing and desiring to You with regards to it. So keep me alive upon that for whatever duration You cause me to live, and cause me to die upon that whenever You cause me to die, and resurrect me upon that whenever You resurrect me.
And if there was a deficiency from me in what is past, then I repent to You from it and wish to You regarding what is in Your Presence.

And I ask You to safeguard me from Your disobedience, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye, ever, for whatever duration You keep me alive, neither less than that nor more. The self is prone to evil except what You are merciful with, O most Merciful of the merciful ones.

And I ask You to safeguard me by Your obedience until You cause me to die upon it and You are pleased with me, and to end for me with happiness, and do not turn me away from it ever. And there is no strength except with You.

key_terms.وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِكَ: And there is no strength except with You

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication to recite after finishing the daily prayer to affirm Wilayah and seek steadfastness?
ai.summary: This supplication, recorded in Al-Kafi, emphasizes the theological concept of 'Adin' (testifying/affirming) through obedience and love for the Prophet and the Twelve Imams, linking spiritual success to their Wilayah. It integrates repentance for past shortcomings with a plea for divine preservation from the 'nafs al-ammara' (commanding self), reflecting the Shia emphasis on continuous self-purification and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings as the path to ultimate felicity.
